title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: WES AND THE BEES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wes Parnell, an insurance claims adjuster in Charleston, South Carolina.
His phone rang sixty times a day. So at forty-five, he bought twenty thousand bees.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PLUG
segments.quote: Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes.
segments.author: Anne Lamott
lines: Wes was snapping at everybody. Even the dog.
His wife Tamika had a fridge magnet from the writer Anne Lamott:
Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes.
Including you, she said, and took his phone.
So, a beehive in the backyard. Thirty minutes a day. No phone.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE STING
segments.quote: Our patience will achieve more than our force.
segments.author: Edmund Burke
lines: The first time, Wes yanked the lid off like he was late for a meeting.
A bee stung his nose. He looked like a sad clown for a week.
Miss Odessa, eighty-two, from the bee club, quoted the statesman Edmund Burke:
Our patience will achieve more than our force.
So Wes learned to move slow and hum. The bees calmed down. So did he.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NEIGHBOR
segments.quote: I never met a man I didn't like.
segments.author: Will Rogers
lines: Then came Gus next door, a retired Navy cook with a voice like a foghorn.
Get those bugs out of here, he yelled, or I'm calling the city!
Wes wanted to yell back. Then he remembered the cowboy humorist Will Rogers:
I never met a man I didn't like.
Well, he'd never really met Gus. So he knocked with two glasses of sweet tea.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SWARM
segments.quote: When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the Universe.
segments.author: John Muir
lines: In June, half the bees swarmed into Gus's oak tree.
But Gus was staring at his garden. His tomatoes had never been so fat.
Wes laughed and quoted the nature writer John Muir:
When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the Universe.
So Gus held the ladder, Wes boxed the swarm, and nobody called the city.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE HONEY
segments.quote: Never does nature say one thing and wisdom another.
segments.author: Juvenal
lines: By August, the hive was heavy with honey. Wes wanted every drop.
Miss Odessa said, leave them enough for winter. Then she quoted the Roman writer Juvenal:
Never does nature say one thing and wisdom another.
So Wes took half. Still, sixty jars. His kitchen floor was sticky until Halloween.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE HIVE
segments.quote: That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: Sixty jars is too much honey for one man.
Tamika read him a line from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee.
So Wes shared honey with the whole street. Gus traded tomatoes. Now there's a Saturday cookout, and Wes's phone stays in the kitchen.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Unplug. Be patient. Meet your neighbor. See the links. Leave enough. Share the honey.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Unplug. Be patient. Meet your neighbor. See the links. Leave enough. Share the honey.
I tried keeping bees once. They held a meeting and voted me out.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
